semantic_correction.stem: A parent asks when a healthy infant should first establish routine preventive dental care. Which recommendation is most consistent with current pediatric dental guidance?

options.A: Schedule the first dental visit after most primary teeth have erupted so the dentist can evaluate the full dentition.
options.B: Wait until preschool unless pain, trauma, or visible decay creates a reason for an earlier dental visit.
options.C: Establish a dental home within 6 months after the first tooth erupts and no later than 12 months of age.
options.D: Plan the first routine dental visit around age 3, when cooperation with a full examination is usually easier.

semantic_correction.rationale: The American Academy of Pediatric Dentistry's 2026–2027 Reference Manual states that a dental home should be established within 6 months of eruption of the first tooth and no later than 12 months of age. Early establishment supports caries-risk assessment, parental education, anticipatory guidance, and preventive oral health care. Waiting for symptoms, completion of primary tooth eruption, preschool age, or age 3 delays preventive care beyond the recommended window.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Teach parents to establish a dental home within 6 months of the first tooth erupting and no later than age 12 months.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item directly tests the current dental-home timing recommendation with no symptom-based or cooperation-based delay.

option_audit.A: Incorrect. Preventive dental care should begin well before most primary teeth have erupted.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. AAPD recommends preventive dental-home establishment before symptoms or preschool age.
option_audit.C: Correct. It exactly matches the current AAPD timing recommendation.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Waiting until age 3 is later than the recommended no-later-than-12-month window.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. C alone reproduces the current AAPD timing recommendation.
cueing_check: All four options are first-dental-visit timing recommendations of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies C.
